```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mediaPlanCopula)
```

## What the model does

`distrib_hybrid_copula()` returns the distribution of the total number of
contacts of a plan from, for each vehicle, the reach of one insertion (`r1`) and
of two insertions (`r2`), the number of insertions, and optionally the
duplication of the first insertions between vehicles. A vehicle with a bounded
number of insertions has a Beta-Binomial marginal (`"bbd"`) and a vehicle that
delivers an unbounded stream of impressions has a Negative Binomial marginal
(`"nbd"`). A Gaussian copula links the vehicles.

## A mixed plan

```{r mixed}
fit <- distrib_hybrid_copula(
  r1 = c(TV = 0.20, Digital = 0.02),
  r2 = c(TV = 0.312, Digital = 0.0390),
  insertions = c(5, 50),
  model_type = c("bbd", "nbd"),
  dup_matrix = matrix(c(0.20, 0.006, 0.006, 0.02), 2),
  n_qmc = 1024
)
fit
```

The reach of one and two insertions of each vehicle is reproduced exactly. The
duplication is calibrated, and the result reports how well:

```{r diag}
fit$diagnostics$pairs
c(reach1_error = fit$diagnostics$reach1_error,
  dup_error = fit$diagnostics$dup_error)
```

## Numerical accuracy

The distribution is integrated with a deterministic quasi-Monte Carlo sample, so
it uses no random numbers. The cost and the accuracy depend on `n_qmc`, and the
accuracy should be checked by comparing two values.

```{r qmc}
a <- distrib_hybrid_copula(c(A = 0.2, B = 0.15), c(0.312, 0.23925), c(5, 5),
                           dup_matrix = matrix(c(0.2, 0.05, 0.05, 0.15), 2),
                           n_qmc = 1024)
b <- distrib_hybrid_copula(c(A = 0.2, B = 0.15), c(0.312, 0.23925), c(5, 5),
                           dup_matrix = matrix(c(0.2, 0.05, 0.05, 0.15), 2),
                           n_qmc = 16384)
0.5 * sum(abs(a$distribution$pmf - b$distribution$pmf))  # total variation
```

## When the duplications cannot be matched

With three or more vehicles, the correlations are calibrated pair by pair, and
the resulting matrix may not be positive definite. The function then adjusts it
and warns, and the fitted duplications differ from the targets. The same happens
when a duplication is not attainable by a Gaussian copula with the given
marginals.

```{r psd}
d <- matrix(c(.2, .065, .025, .065, .2, .065, .025, .065, .2), 3)
msg <- character()
f <- withCallingHandlers(
  distrib_gcbbd(rep(0.2, 3), rep(0.312, 3), c(3, 3, 3), d, n_qmc = 512),
  warning = function(w) {
    msg <<- c(msg, conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  })
msg
f$diagnostics$psd_adjusted
round(f$diagnostics$dup_error, 4)
```

`diagnostics$dup_error` is the largest absolute error in a duplication, in
proportions. Report it together with any result built on a plan whose
duplications were adjusted.

## What the inputs do not determine

The reach of one and two insertions and the duplication do not determine the
distribution of contacts. The shape beyond them comes from the assumptions of the
model: Beta or Gamma propensities, a Gaussian copula, and exchangeable
insertions within a vehicle. Models with the same inputs and different
assumptions give different distributions, and comparisons with other
multivehicle models on survey-derived data showed small differences in accuracy
that were not stable out of sample. The model is therefore offered as an
implementation that is available for every plan and that reports its own
calibration error, and not as a more accurate alternative to other models.

To study how a model behaves under mechanisms with a known truth, see the
`mediaPlanSim` package, which generates synthetic exposure data and the true
distribution of contacts.
